title: U-Net
description: Symmetric encoder-decoder network utilizing skip-links for precise pixel segmentation mapping.
name: U-Net
summary: U-Net is a convolutional network architecture designed for fast and precise image segmentation. It consists of a contracting path (encoder) to capture context and a symmetric expanding path (decoder) with skip connections to enable precise localization.
use_when: Performing pixel-level image segmentation, especially in biomedical imaging or satellite analysis.
avoid_when: Working with general image classification or bounding-box detection tasks without pixel-level map needs.
pros: Skip connections preserve high-resolution spatial details in outputs.
Can be trained successfully with relatively small annotated image sets.
End-to-end pixel mapping supports arbitrary input shapes.
cons: Requires substantial memory footprint due to skip connection feature map duplication.
Cannot capture global contextual relationships natively due to localized convolutions.
Sensitive to boundary alignment artifacts during pooling.

key_hyperparams.name: bilinear
key_hyperparams.note: Whether to use bilinear upsampling instead of transposed convolutions to prevent checkerboard artifacts.
